title: Vendor onboarding: scope & MSA routing call
summary: Kickoff to align on vendor onboarding path for Redwood Inference. Primary focus: MSA redlines, DPA language for data residency, SLA targets for Dedicated vs Hosted, and billing/entitlements clarification. Legal wants minimal exceptions; procurement needs pricing approval path and pilot acceptance criteria. Agreed next steps: Evan to share MSA redline template and SOC2 + KMS docs, Samira to run technical preflight checklist and propose SLA numbers for a 90-day pilot, customer to supply contract owner and timeline for approvals.
next_steps: Evan: send MSA redline and DPA template + SOC2 + KMS note (by 2026-11-20)
Samira: share proposed SLA table and pilot runbook (by 2026-11-18)
Customer: confirm legal review owner and internal procurement timeline (by 2026-11-17)
Schedule security deep dive with Karen & Samira (target week of 2026-11-22)

Samira - prepare SLA heatmap (p99 latency, availability SLOs, credit calc) and pilot ops checklist - due 2026-11-18

transcript:
Meeting: Vendor onboarding: scope & MSA routing call
Date/Time: 2026-11-13 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Evan Price (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Ishaan Verma (Redwood CSM), Mohan Patel (Crestpoint Procurement), Karen Liu (Crestpoint InfoSec), Diego Ruiz (Crestpoint Eng), Lena Thompson (Crestpoint Legal), Aria Gomez (Product)

--- Optional auto-summary present above ---

00:00 Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro: I'm Evan, I'll be your AE for this onboarding path, Samira is our SE, Ishaan will be support during the pilot. We wanted to use this call to align on the contractual path, technical preflight, and what a 90-day pilot acceptance looks like.
00:32 Mohan (Procurement): Thanks Evan. High level, procurement wants to understand the MSA route, what exceptions we need to open, and who signs. We also need estimate of costs for the pilot and how it maps to our budget approval cycle.
01:05 Karen (InfoSec): And from security side, we need to understand data residency, KMS options, audit logs, and whether we can get a SOC2 or ISO package up front. Also, any on-prem or VPC options matter.
01:40 Samira (Redwood SE): Totally. On the platform side, Redwood offers hosted, dedicated (reserved GPUs) and private deployments. For pilot we often recommend Dedicated so you get predictable latency; but if data residency is a hard stop, Redwood Private can be discussed — it has different commercial implications.
02:10 Lena (Legal): For legal, our immediate ask is to see your standard MSA and DPA and call out any non-starters. We will run redlines through our counsel.
02:35 Evan: Understood. We'll share the MSA/DPA templates and a redline guide. Two notes: 1) we typically limit indemnity changes at enterprise deals; 2) data retention and deletion clauses are frequent asks.
03:05 Diego (Engineering): From an engineering preflight, can you outline network egress requirements, SSO integration (SAML/OIDC), and whether we can rotate KMS keys on our side?
03:40 Samira: For SSO we support SAML and OIDC; we integrate with enterprise IdPs. KMS: for Redwood Private, you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS. For hosted, we offer customer-specific encryption at rest with managed KMS, and we have a KMS integration option for Dedicated customers — there are trade-offs that we'll detail.
04:15 Mohan: Pricing path — does Redwood require committed spend for Dedicated during a pilot? Procurement needs options where we can run a pilot without heavy commit.
04:40 Evan: We can structure a time-bound pilot on Dedicated with a short-term reservation or a burstable plan. If procurement needs zero-commit, hosted API is the fallback but won't satisfy data residency. We'll include pricing scenarios in the follow-up.
05:12 Lena: A few legal specifics: we prefer 90-day notice for termination, standard data processor terms, and explicit audit rights. We may want to limit subprocessor transfers.
05:40 Evan: Noted. We usually allow audit via SOC2 + on-site audit for enterprise deals; DPA allows subprocessor lists and customer review. We'll attach our subprocessors list — but it's often redlined.
06:10 Karen: What about logs — do you provide token-level audit logs and query-level tracing? We need forensic capability for regulated data.
06:35 Samira: Yes, Console gives per-route latency/cost breakdowns and request-level traces for the retention window. Retention windows are configurable in Private; hosted has default retention policy — we'll document exact windows.
07:05 Mohan: Timeline question — we need procurement signoff before our December board freeze. Is that doable?
07:25 Evan: Tight but possible if legal and security have quick reads. That's why we're pushing docs right away. If we get redline back in a week, we can move fast.
08:00 Diego: Pilot acceptance criteria — what metrics will we use? Latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rates, and functional correctness (test prompts).
08:30 Samira: Agreed. We'll propose an acceptance matrix: p99 under X ms for 512 token prompts on Dedicated, availability > 99.9%, and zero PII leakage on evaluation prompt suite. We'll also provide a regression suite for quality checks.
09:10 Karen: PII / data residency — Crestpoint cannot send unmasked PHI outside EU data centers for the initial pilot. Can Redwood guarantee EU-only processing?
09:35 Samira: We have region pinning and can route requests to EU capacity. For hosted we have EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private in your VPC or our private deployment. We'll outline the differences in the doc set.
10:05 Lena: On liability caps and indemnity, we're likely to push for higher caps for material breaches affecting data. How flexible is that?
10:28 Evan: We're open to negotiating commercial caps but that typically maps to commitment level and pricing. We'll propose a modest increase for pilot-sized commitments.
10:55 Mohan: Procurement also needs clarity on billing and entitlements: are there seat counts, token-based bills, or throughput tiers? We need an estimate per-month for the pilot.
11:20 Ishaan (CSM): Billing can be usage-based (tokens/embedding units) or reserved capacity for Dedicated. We'll outline a pilot SKU that mixes a small reservation plus overage at a discounted rate.
11:55 Diego: Also, can we run test benchmarks to compare Redwood Dedicated vs our in-house inference? We need throughput/latency tables.
12:20 Samira: Yes — we can run a benchmark in a side-by-side config. We'll need a small dataset and access to your test harness; Samira to run this with Diego during the pilot.
12:48 Aria (PM): Who will be the signatory on the Crestpoint side? Procurement will route to the head of engineering or CFO?
13:05 Mohan: Procurement will own the routing but final signatory is likely Head of Engineering for technical pilots. We'll confirm.
13:30 Evan: Good. Next, on subprocessors and KMS: Karen, you mentioned wanting BYOK. For BYOK on Private we support HSM integration. For Dedicated, there are options but full BYOK means additional controls. We'll document specifics.
14:02 Karen: Also need clarity on vulnerability disclosure and mitigation timelines. We ask for SLA for critical CVEs.
14:28 Samira: We publish PSIRT timelines and commit to patches for critical severity within agreed windows for enterprise plans. We'll share the PSIRT doc.
15:00 Lena: MSA redlines — we will likely propose edits to data retention, audit rights, and liability sections. Can you take our redlines and provide a comment matrix?
15:25 Evan: Yes, we'll create a comment matrix mapping your redline to our standard position and proposed compromise. That speeds review cycles.
15:50 Mohan: Procurement: if we agree to a 90-day pilot with a small committed tranche, can we get a 'trial discount' applied to the first three months?
16:12 Evan: We can include a pilot discount; we'll outline exact numbers in the pricing sheet.
16:40 Diego: Integration work — we estimate two sprints for SSO + networking + test harness. Will Redwood provide an integration checklist and runbook?
17:05 Ishaan: Yes, we'll provide a runbook and dedicated onboarding slack channel. We'll also assign a technical onboarding engineer for the pilot.
17:40 Karen: Regarding encryption in transit and at rest, we need TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest. Also key rotation policy.
18:03 Samira: TLS 1.2+ supported, default AES-256. Key rotation supported in Private and some Dedicated configurations. We'll include the rotation schedule and API for key rotation.
18:35 Lena: Do you contractually accept right-to-audit with a 30-day notice?
18:50 Evan: We accept audits via SOC2 plus procedural on-site audits with reasonable notice; exact notice period we'll propose — typically 30-60 days.
19:20 Mohan: Who owns the support escalation path during pilot? We need tiered SLAs and a named contact.
19:40 Ishaan: We'll provide 24/7 support for Severity 1 during pilot for enterprise customers with an assigned TAM. Ishaan will act as primary CSM contact.
20:10 Aria: A technical question — do you support model pinning and rollback in your rollout policies? We need deterministic behavior for production experiments.
20:35 Samira: Yes, model version pinning and canary rollouts are supported. We also have automatic fallback to compatible variants in case of failures.
21:00 Diego: Any export controls or data transfer constraints we should be aware of?
21:20 Samira: We'll document data transfer routing and any export control notes, especially if you plan to use models trained on restricted corpora.
21:45 Mohan: Timeline again — assuming we get the docs today and legal sends redlines in a week, do you think a Nov 29 start date for pilot is realistic?
22:05 Evan: Yes, Nov 29 start looks doable if we keep to the follow-ups.
22:30 Lena: For DPA, we will need specific language on subprocessor notifications and deletion certification at project close.
22:55 Evan: We'll include deletion certification language and a standard subprocessors clause; if you need more restrictive terms we can discuss exceptions.
23:25 Karen: Also interested in penetration test reports and third-party pen test cadence.
23:50 Samira: We have annual pen tests and can share redacted reports under NDA.
24:10 Diego: On the SLA table — could you propose a credit formula for availability misses? Engineering wants to know the math.
24:38 Samira: Absolutely, we'll propose standard credit calc (pro rata based on downtime buckets) and also a separate performance SLA tied to p99 latency.
25:05 Mohan: Any references/customers in our vertical you can share for procurement comfort?
25:28 Evan: We can share anonymized references and case studies; we'll propose two references with similar security posture.
25:55 Aria: If we run into legal exceptions that Redwood cannot accept, what's the escalation path?
26:12 Evan: We'll escalate to our commercial legal and CSM; Ishaan will coordinate. Commercial exceptions sometimes require exec approval — we'll flag those early.
26:40 Diego: For the benchmark, Samira, can you outline required artifacts from our side? e.g., test harness, expected QPS, sample prompts.
27:00 Samira: Need your test harness access, sample prompt set, desired latency shape, and network whitelist for our test agents. We'll send a checklist.
27:28 Lena: Quick note — Crestpoint legal may request a 45-day review window for the first pass of MSA redlines. Expect that from us.
27:50 Evan: Okay noted; we'll plan milestones accordingly.
28:20 Mohan: Procurement want two pricing pathways: minimal commit + pilot, and committed dedicated for production. We'll need both in the pricing pack.
28:45 Evan: We'll provide both; pricing will show pilot discount and committed capacity math.
29:10 Karen: Also, we may ask for role-based access controls (RBAC) mapping for our team so we can provision limited access for the product team, and stricter access for legal/procurement.
29:30 Ishaan: RBAC is supported in Console; we'll include a mapping example.
30:00 Aria: If data residency is hard requirement, do we need on-prem or is VPC_private enough?
30:20 Samira: VPC-private (Redwood Private) is often sufficient if you can accept our software stack inside your network or dedicated customer VPC. On-prem is possible but has longer lead times.
30:55 Lena: Can you confirm who signs the DPA? Is it an addendum to the MSA or separate?
31:15 Evan: DPA typically is an addendum; we can also put it inline if you prefer. We'll send DPA as a separate doc for ease of redline.
31:40 Diego: Operationally, what's the expected time to stand up Dedicated test pool?
31:58 Samira: For Dedicated in our shared capacity pools, provisioning is 48-72 hours once billing is confirmed. For reserved Dedicated capacity that needs physical GPU ordering, it can be longer. We'll specify.
32:25 Mohan: Procurement wants visibility on invoice cadence and any late payment penalties.
32:40 Evan: We'll state net-30 standard, with negotiated terms for enterprise. Late penalties are negotiable but we'll include standard language in the pricing doc.
33:10 Lena: Please include audit log retention window options and costs for extended retention.
33:30 Ishaan: We'll provide pricing for 90/180/365 day retention tiers.
34:00 Karen: A note: Crestpoint requires data localization in EU for pilot, and at least EU-only processing for initial dataset. We need a guarantee.
34:22 Samira: We'll propose routing rules and show capacity availability in EU. If accepted, we'll add that to the DPA.
34:50 Diego: On integration, we may need IP allowlists — can you support static IPs for outbound egress?
35:10 Samira: We can provide egress IP ranges for Dedicated/private deployments. Hosted egress ranges are wider; we'll detail in the network appendix.
35:45 Mohan: Any SLA on response time for procurement questions?
36:00 Evan: We'll commit to 48 business hours for procurement queries and faster for legal/security escalations.
36:30 Aria: If we decide to go with Private, what are the expected onboarding costs?
36:50 Evan: Onboarding costs depend on footprint. We'll include a rough estimate in the follow-up — typically an initial one-time onboarding fee plus recurring infra cost.
37:20 Lena: For contract redlines, if we can't get agreement on a clause, can we use an exceptions tracker to surface to our execs quickly?
37:40 Evan: Yes, we'll produce an exceptions tracker mapping clause, customer ask, Redwood position, and commercial tie. That will be in the comment matrix.
38:10 Diego: Security deep dive — we want to schedule it with Karen and Samira next week.
38:30 Karen: I can do Tuesday or Thursday afternoon UTC.
38:45 Samira: I'll send a Doodle for next week and propose Tue/Thu windows.
39:05 Ishaan: Also creating the pilot Slack channel and inviting Crestpoint team.
39:20 Evan: Great. Are there any non-starters we haven't covered?
39:32 Lena: Not from legal today; main ask is that we see the MSA and DPA.
39:45 Mohan: Procurement just wants timelines and pilot price.
39:55 Aria: Engineering wants benchmark plan.
40:10 Evan: Ok to recap quick then next steps.
40:18 Evan: Recap - Evan will send MSA+DPA+SOC2+KMS doc, Samira will produce SLA heatmap and benchmark runbook, Ishaan will set up onboarding channel and TAM assignment, customer will confirm contract owner and timeline.
40:45 Mohan: Sounds good.
41:00 Lena: We'll aim to return redlines in about a week, but expect legal review may take 10-14 business days.
41:20 Ishaan: I'll own the pilot kickoff coordination and will propose dates once we have redlines.
41:40 Samira: I'll also attach a small prompt set for the regression check and a network checklist.
42:05 Evan: Any final Qs?
42:15 Diego: No, we're good.
42:22 Aria: No.
42:25 Karen: No.
42:30 Evan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc packet and schedule the security deep dive.
42:45 Mohan: Thanks team.
43:00 Meeting end.

--- Notes about transcription quality: speaker turns are accurate though occasional mishears (Redwood Private spelled sometimes). Natural speech present with interruptions and clarifications. ---
notes: Shared artifacts to be attached in follow-up: MSA template, DPA template, SOC2 report (redacted), KMS integration note, SLA heatmap, pilot runbook
Security deep dive to be scheduled (Karen + Samira)
